title: These 35 States Are Deciding Who’ll Run Their Elections
author: Camille Squires
content:
Upon retaking the White House, Donald Trump demanded that states share
sensitive voter data with federal agencies—a key step in his broader project
of controlling and manipulating election administration.

Ohio Secretary of State Frank LaRose complied, saying he “absolutely wants
more collaboration” with the feds. Iowa Secretary of State Paul Pate, a
Republican like LaRose, complied as well, saying he’d been “persuaded” that
the Trump administration would take good care of the data. Another [14
states](https://www.brennancenter.org/our-work/research-reports/tracker-
justice-department-requests-voter-information), all of which have Republicans
in charge of elections, [joined](https://stateline.org/2025/09/18/some-
republican-states-resist-doj-demand-for-private-voter-data/) in compliance.

However, many other secretaries rebuffed Trump’s demands, like Minnesota’s
Steve Simon and Nevada’s Cisco Aguilar, both Democrats. The federal government
sued those states, but courts have largely upheld their refusal to comply.

These states, and many others, are choosing a new elections chief in November.
Trump’s bid to control voting information and procedures looms over all of
them.

In Iowa, for instance, Democrat Ryan Peterman, who is running against Pate,
vows to reject data-sharing with the White House. “I will treat Iowans’
information as what it is: theirs,” he promises. In Ohio, Democratic secretary
of state candidate Allison Russo promises the same: “Protecting this data is
essential,” she says.

All in all, 35 states, plus D.C., are voting in November, directly or
indirectly, on who runs their elections. In 23 states, voters are doing this
directly by electing the public official—typically the secretary of state—who
will oversee elections. In another 12 states and D.C., voters are selecting
the officials who will then appoint their state elections chiefs.

These contests will shape what election administration looks like in critical
swing states, and decide who is actually running election mechanics in 2028,
the next presidential cycle.

![Map of states with elections chief elections.](https://boltsmag.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/10/ElectionsChief2026-2400x1546.jpg)

Data-sharing is but one fault line in these contests, which are also defined
by [ongoing turmoil](https://boltsmag.org/mail-voting-your-questions-
answered/) around mail voting, a method the GOP has looked to restrict, and by
continued efforts from Trump allies who falsely deny his 2020 loss and have
pushed to take over elections.

Election deniers are, once again, running to oversee elections in the swing
states of Arizona and Nevada. Arizona’s contest features Republican Alexander
Kolodin, who was disciplined by the Arizona State Bar for his role in a
lawsuit trying to overturn the 2020 results, and Nevada’s features Republican
Jim Marchant, who wants to unregister every voter in the state.

The race for Arizona secretary of state is especially significant; this office
[will be tasked](https://boltsmag.org/whats-on-the-ballot/who-counts-our-
elections/#AZ) with certifying the results of the 2028 presidential race.

A host of other Republican candidates have also mirrored Trump’s priorities on
voting. There’s Pat Proctor in Kansas, who last year
[sponsored](https://boltsmag.org/restrictions-on-grace-periods-for-mail-
ballots/) legislation that eliminated the state’s grace period for mail
ballots, as Trump has demanded. There’s Tim Fleming in Georgia, who says the
2020 election was marred with “irregularities” and who wants to severely
restrict mail voting. There’s Robert Sprague in Ohio, whose ads say he would
“ditch” ballot drop boxes as evidence of his support for Trump.

But these offices also matter in more subtle but important ways. Elections
leaders can influence whether citizen initiatives make the ballot. They have
the power to help the most marginalized in the electorate register and cast a
ballot, or can choose to make that process more difficult. They often set the
scale of voter roll purges.

Even where they can’t unilaterally change voting procedures, they are often
major players in state legislative debates on all manners on election policy.

In Colorado, for instance, Democratic secretary of state nominee Amanda
Gonzalez [helped author](https://boltsmag.org/colorado-voting-centers-in-
jails-bill/) a landmark law to require polling places in local jails, and she
told _Bolts_ she plans to advocate for continued expansion of voting access
for incarcerated people.

In Wyoming, Republican secretary of state nominee Robert Short
[vows](https://boltsmag.org/wyoming-gop-primary-secretary-of-state-freedom-
caucus/) to advocate for finally allowing online voter registration, which
nearly all other states already have.

Explore our state-by-state breakdown of the 2026 midterms below.

Key contests to watch include [Georgia](https://boltsmag.org/guide-to-
contests-for-chief-elections-official-secretary-of-state/#GA), where voters
will choose Brad Raffensperger’s successor, six years after he rebuffed
Trump’s call to “find” him more votes. Democratic incumbents are seeking
reelection in swing [Arizona](https://boltsmag.org/guide-to-contests-for-
chief-elections-official-secretary-of-state/#AZ),
[Minnesota](https://boltsmag.org/guide-to-contests-for-chief-elections-
official-secretary-of-state/#MN), and [Nevada](https://boltsmag.org/guide-to-
contests-for-chief-elections-official-secretary-of-state/#NV), and a GOP
incumbent is seeking a fourth term in [Iowa](https://boltsmag.org/guide-to-
contests-for-chief-elections-official-secretary-of-state/IA).

Meanwhile, [Colorado](https://boltsmag.org/guide-to-contests-for-chief-
elections-official-secretary-of-state/#CO),
[Indiana](https://boltsmag.org/guide-to-contests-for-chief-elections-official-
secretary-of-state/#IN), [Kansas](https://boltsmag.org/guide-to-contests-for-
chief-elections-official-secretary-of-state/#KS),
[Michigan](https://boltsmag.org/guide-to-contests-for-chief-elections-
official-secretary-of-state/#MI), [New Mexico](https://boltsmag.org/guide-to-
contests-for-chief-elections-official-secretary-of-state/#NM),
[Nebraska](https://boltsmag.org/guide-to-contests-for-chief-elections-
official-secretary-of-state/#NE), and [Ohio](https://boltsmag.org/guide-to-
contests-for-chief-elections-official-secretary-of-state/#OH) are all electing
new secretaries of state in open and possibly competitive contests.

And in [Florida](https://boltsmag.org/guide-to-contests-for-chief-elections-
official-secretary-of-state/#FL) and [Texas](https://boltsmag.org/guide-to-
contests-for-chief-elections-official-secretary-of-state/#TX), the winner of
unexpectedly tight governor races will get to appoint the next secretary of
state.

For more information on the workings of election administration, you can
explore _Bolts_ ’ state-by-state databases. The first, [Who Runs our
Elections?](https://boltsmag.org/whats-on-the-ballot/local-election-
administration/), details which state offices prepare and administer an
election. The second, [Who Counts Our Elections?](https://boltsmag.org/whats-
on-the-ballot/who-counts-our-elections/) details which state offices handle
the counting, canvassing, and certification stages.

### **Alabama**

**Via election for secretary of state**

Alabama Secretary of State Wes Allen courted much controversy in that role,
[pulling the state out of ERIC,](https://boltsmag.org/alabama-secretary-of-
state-leaves-eric/) the multi-state project for sharing voter data that was
used to keep voter rolls clean and detect fraud, and [threatening to
keep](https://alabamareflector.com/2024/04/22/wes-allen-joe-biden/) Joe Biden
off Alabama’s ballot in 2024. Now that he is retiring to run for lieutenant
governor, Republican Caroleene Dobson and Democrat Wayne Rogers are running to
replace him.

Dobson, an attorney, claimed during her successful run in the GOP primary that
voter fraud is a major threat and [she has said she wants to create a
centralized unit](https://yellowhammernews.com/caroleene-dobson-we-still-have-
a-lot-of-work-to-do-when-it-comes-to-election-integrity/) dedicated to
investigating elections modeled after Florida’s. Florida
[created](https://boltsmag.org/florida-new-police-force/) such an office in
2022 and then [prosecuted](https://boltsmag.org/desantis-voter-arrests-
amendment-4/) residents who made voting errors. Rogers, the underdog in this
red state, is running on the need to adopt an “Alabama Voting Rights Act” to
replace [gutted](https://boltsmag.org/scotus-callais-voting-rights-act-ask-
bolts/) federal protections.

Alabama is [one of just three states that doesn’t allow any in-person early
voting](https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/early-in-person-voting)
_; The Alabama Reflector_ [reports that only
Rogers](https://alabamareflector.com/2026/09/28/rogers-dobson-lay-out-
contrasting-plans-for-alabama-secretary-of-states-office/) has said he is in
favor of changing that.

### **Alaska**

**Via election for governor and lieutenant governor**

In Alaska, the lieutenant governor, who is selected by a gubernatorial
candidate and then elected on a joint ticket with that candidate, oversees
elections and appoints the state’s elections director.

For the past four years, Republican Lieutenant Governor Nancy Dahlstrom has
been the state’s elections supervisor, but she’ll exit office after the
election, replaced by one of four people in what [polling
shows](https://alaskapublic.org/news/politics/elections/2026-09-22/poll-shows-
democrat-with-lead-in-alaska-governors-race-but-large-swaths-remain-undecided)
is a close November race for governor and lieutenant governor. The field
features one Democrat and three Republicans, and it will be decided by ranked-
choice voting.

Whoever takes over Alaska elections will have at least one big issue to work
on, if they care to: in recent years, the state has prosecuted American
Samoans for voting after they were erroneously registered to vote, [as _Bolts_
reported in January](https://boltsmag.org/prosecuted-for-voting-american-
samoans-alaska/). American Samoans are U.S. nationals who do not have the
right to vote in U.S. elections, and while the state [dismissed those charges
in September](https://boltsmag.org/charges-dropped-against-american-samoans-
punished-for-voting-in-alaska/), the porous voter registration systems and
resulting mass confusion that made the case possible to begin with still
largely remain.

### **Arizona**

**Via election for secretary of state**

Adrian Fontes, a Democrat who once ran elections in Maricopa County, is
seeking a second term in a state that is a
[perennial](https://boltsmag.org/secretary-of-state-races-election-deniers-
results/) [battleground](https://boltsmag.org/maricopa-county-election-
administration-2024-results/) over election administration: Each of Arizona’s
last three secretary of state elections has been decided by five points or
fewer.

Fontes has spent much of his time in office defending against the White
House’s attempt to seize control of state-level election administration—and
his Republican opponent in November, Alexander Kolodin, is a loyal soldier in
that effort. A far-right state representative from Scottsdale, Kolodin was an
attorney in Trump’s failed 2020 suit to overturn his defeat that year in
Arizona. The Arizona Supreme Court [later
found](https://azmirror.com/2023/12/14/gop-lawmaker-alexander-kolodin-
sanctioned-for-2020-kraken-lawsuit-other-election-cases/) Kolodin had
“violated his duty to the legal profession” by arguing to overturn results
despite lacking evidence, and the State Bar of Arizona [disciplined
Kolodin](https://www.kjzz.org/2023-12-15/content-1865727-state-bar-
disciplines-arizona-lawmaker-who-represented-fake-electors) for his actions
related to the 2020 election.

![](https://boltsmag.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/10/25168661883126-scaled.jpg)Alexander Kolodin speaks in
the Arizona House on April 23, 2025 (AP Photo/Samantha Chow).

In parallel with his work to assist Trump, Kolodin’s been active in state-
level election matters. He filed a lawsuit in 2022—[also
unsuccessful](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/elections/arizona-supreme-
court-rejects-gop-request-invalidate-mail-voting-rcna23139)—to end mail-in
voting in Arizona. This year, as a lawmaker, Kolodin led the effort to advance
a ballot measure, [Proposition 144](https://azmirror.com/voter-guides/ballot-
measures/proposition-144/), that, among other changes, proposes strict new
voter ID requirements and codifies the state law excluding non-citizens from
voting.  

Fontes, by contrast, [defends vote-by-mail](https://azsos.gov/news/1067),
which he has called “not only secure, but one of the easiest ways to expand
access to voting, increase participation in our elections, and ensure that
every eligible voter in the state can vote.” He denied the Department of
Justice’s request for state voter roll information and then successfully
fought the GOP’s lawsuit to access that data, and he joined another lawsuit
opposing the failed federal bid to overhaul mail voting rules through the
United States Postal Service. When the Department of Homeland Security
[threatened](https://www.ms.now/news/dhs-secretary-mullin-speaks-on-efforts-
to-support-election-security-after-trump-speech) to withhold federal funding
to states that do not accept its proposed election reforms, Fontes said that
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin could “[suck on a salt
lick](https://azmirror.com/2026/07/17/suck-on-a-salt-lick-fontes-fires-back-
after-trump-election-speech-dhs-pressure-on-states/).”

### **Arkansas**

**Via election for secretary of state**

Kim Hammer, a Republican state senator, sponsored a [barrage of
laws](https://boltsmag.org/new-rules-from-gop-legislature-target-arkansas-
ballot-initiatives/) last year that created new hurdles for citizen-led
initiatives. His proposals gave the secretary of state’s office new powers to
disqualify ballot measures. A local advocate who has organized initiatives in
Arkansas, Melissa Fults, [told _Bolts_ at the time](https://boltsmag.org/new-
rules-from-gop-legislature-target-arkansas-ballot-initiatives/) that the new
laws will transform the secretary of state into “judge, jury and executioner
for the petitioning process.”

Hammer is now running for secretary of state, the office whose powers he
helped extend. He is the frontrunner against Democrat Kelly Grappe, the
founder of a civic engagement [nonprofit](https://standuparkansas.com/) who
also works in marketing. Grappe has criticized the changes that have
restricted direct democracy. “I believe that role should amplify the power of
the people and empower the people,” she told local press as she [launched her
bid last fall](https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2025/oct/31/democrat-kelly-
grappe-announces-for-secretary-of/).

### **California**

**Via election for secretary of state**

Secretary of State Shirley Weber is running for reelection and is favored to
win over Republican Donald Wagner, a supervisor in Orange County. Weber
finished 22 points ahead of Wagner in the all-party primary in June, but the
two must face off again in November.

The candidates disagree on the biggest election-related issue on California’s
ballot, [Proposition 39](https://abc7.com/post/what-know-
proposition-39-californias-voter-id-measure/19872464/), which would require
people to present an approved government-issued ID at the polls. Weber opposes
the measure, telling KQED, “Oftentimes those things are put in place merely to
deter people from voting, to make it more difficult for people to vote.” Data
from other states [show](https://www.wpr.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/mayer-
decrescenzo-2019-voter-identification-and-nonvoting-in-wisconsin-evidence-
from-the-2016-election-003.pdf) that similar measures have suppressed voting.

Wagner supports Proposition 39, [saying](https://www.kcra.com/article/don-
wagner-explains-why-he-should-be-californias-next-secretary-of-state-ca-
politics-360/73999511) “it's not going to stop anybody from voting.” He has
said that although he believes elections are broadly fair, there are election
integrity issues “across the spectrum.” Wagner has also called for speeding up
California’s notoriously slow vote tabulation process; he [wants to
allow](https://www.kqed.org/news/12101263/as-trump-targets-elections-
california-will-pick-its-next-secretary-of-state) counties to begin counting
mail ballots before election day, and require counties to publish results
within 72 hours of an election.

### **Colorado**

**Via election for secretary of state**

Democrat Amanda Gonzalez faces Republican James Wiley in the race to replace
two-term Democratic Secretary of State Jena Griswold, who is now running for
state attorney general.

Gonzalez currently oversees elections in populous, suburban Jefferson County,
and before that she ran the Colorado branch of the national voting rights
group Common Cause. She has for many years been a key figure in turning
Colorado into one of the most accessible states for voters, helping to author
plenty of legislation aimed at protecting and expanding voter rights.

This includes a landmark reform bill, [adopted in
2024](https://boltsmag.org/colorado-voting-centers-in-jails-bill/), that made
Colorado the first state to require in-person polling places inside county
jails; most people held in jail were already eligible but faced major barriers
to voting. _Bolts_ [found that the reform sent turnout
soaring](https://boltsmag.org/jail-voting-soars-in-colorado/) in the 2024
elections. Gonzalez tells _Bolts_ she’ll continue working to improve jail-
based turnout, if elected.

![](https://boltsmag.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/IMG_0219.jpg)Someone casts
their ballot inside the Jefferson County jail on Nov. 5, 2024. (Photo courtesy
Jefferson County Clerk's Office)

Wiley, a 2024 minor candidate for Congress and the former director of the
state’s Libertarian Party, opposes Colorado’s universal mail voting program.
He is also a [staunch supporter of Tina
Peters](https://www.courthousenews.com/libertarian-party-of-colorado-sues-to-
remove-secretary-of-state-following-password-leak/), the former county clerk
and Trump ally who was convicted of leaking sensitive elections information,
and who is now reportedly [advising
Trump](https://www.democracydocket.com/news-alerts/election-deniers-cleta-
mitchell-and-tina-peters-want-trumps-commerce-secretary-to-regulate-voting-
machines/) to interfere with midterm voting.

### **Connecticut**

**Via election for secretary of state**

Secretary of State Stephanie Thomas, a Democrat, is running for a second term
against Peter Lumaj, a Republican who has run unsuccessfully for state and
national offices, including secretary of state, [several times in the
past](https://www.ctinsider.com/news/article/Dems-GOP-at-odds-over-proposed-
changes-to-12016643.php).

“Voter fraud is the favorite pastime of the Democratic Party,” Lumaj
[declared](https://www.ctinsider.com/news/article/Dems-GOP-at-odds-over-
proposed-changes-to-12016643.php) in a past campaign for secretary of state.
This year, Lumaj has [pointed to the Trump administration’s
investigations](https://ctnewsjunkie.com/2026/09/03/not-professional-
administration-lumaj-slams-thomas-voter-reassurance-press-conference/) into
elections in many Democratic-run states, including Connecticut, as evidence of
“repeated incompetence.” Thomas, meanwhile, has [rebuffed Trump’s
accusations](https://ctmirror.org/2026/07/20/ct-officials-rebut-presidents-
claims-about-stolen-elections) and urged confidence in election processes.

### **Florida**

**Via election for governor  **

This office is an appointed one, so the next secretary of state will be
decided by the winner of the governor’s race between Republican Byron Donalds,
a staunch Trump ally, and Democrat David Jolly, who is running on rolling back
[recent](https://boltsmag.org/florida-new-restrictions-on-ballot-initiative-
process/) [restrictions](https://boltsmag.org/florida-republicans-immigration-
deal/) and expanding ballot access.

Florida’s current secretary of state, Cord Byrd, [has refused to
acknowledge](https://www.tampabay.com/news/florida-
politics/2022/05/24/florida-elections-chief-cord-byrd-more-elections-changes-
could-be-necessary/) that Biden won in 2020, has mirrored baseless claims
about rampant voter fraud, and has withdrawn Florida from an election security
program targeted by [right-wing conspiracy
theories](https://boltsmag.org/alabama-secretary-of-state-leaves-eric/). He
has also overseen an office created under Governor Ron DeSantis to police
elections, which [rained harsh criminal
charges](https://boltsmag.org/desantis-voter-arrests-amendment-4/) on people
who mistakenly voted despite past felony convictions; most of the cases ended
up [falling apart](https://www.clickorlando.com/news/politics/2023/02/13/case-
dropped-against-orange-county-man-arrested-accused-of-voter-fraud-by-the-
state/).

### **Georgia**

**Via election for secretary of state**

Secretaries of state are usually not celebrities, but Georgia Republican Brad
Raffensperger became a household name in 2020, when he refused Trump’s
[infamous request](https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/trump-
raffensperger-call-georgia-vote/2021/01/03/d45acb92-4dc4-11eb-
bda4-615aaefd0555_story.html) to “find” the thousands of votes he would have
needed to win the state that year.

Raffensperger is term-limited and will be replaced by either Democrat Penny
Reynolds Brown, a former Fulton County judge and [one-time court television
personality](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1139179/), or Republican Tim
Fleming, a state representative who was once chief of staff to outgoing
Governor Brian Kemp.

While Raffensberger defended the integrity of the 2020 election, Fleming [said
at a debate](https://www.pbs.org/video/georgia-secretary-of-state-republicans-
i-atlanta-press-club-debates-sqpf7p/) this spring that there were
“irregularities” that year. He also said “mail and absentee ballots is where
the fraud is” and that he wants to eliminate no-excuse mail voting; as a state
lawmaker, he already sponsored [legislation ](https://www.scrippsnews.com/us-
news/how-voting-laws-have-changed-in-georgia-since-2020)to limit drop boxes.
He also [pushed](https://www.newsfromthestates.com/article/georgia-senate-gop-
muscles-through-election-overhaul-allow-hand-marked-paper-ballots) for Georgia
to withdraw from ERIC, the multi-state data-sharing project that is meant to
detect fraud but was targeted by right-wing conspiracy theories.

Reynolds Brown, who [wants](https://apnews.com/article/judge-penny-brown-
reynolds-georgia-secretary-of-state-40411fb89810b5588e0d2eaf9c1d8e23) to
expand early voting and ballot dropboxes, is trying to become the first
Democrat in 20 years to hold this office, amid a general push by Democrats to
gain ground in this now-swing state.

### **Idaho**

**Via election for secretary of state**

When Republican Phil McGrane won the secretary of state's office in
[2022](https://boltsmag.org/guide-to-2022-secretary-of-state-elections/#ID),
he defeated several fervent election deniers but also refused to affirm that
Joe Biden had won the 2020 election [in an interview with
_Bolts_](https://boltsmag.org/idaho-secretary-of-state-primary/). In office,
he has [defended](https://voteidaho.gov/press-release/idaho-supreme-court-
affirms-new-voter-registration-and-id-laws/) stricter voting procedures from a
[legal challenge](https://idahocapitalsun.com/2024/04/11/idaho-voter-
identification-lawsuit-comes-to-an-end-after-idaho-supreme-court-ruling/),
including a ban on student IDs. This year, he
[supported](https://gemstatechronicle.com/2026/04/mcgrane-voter-fraud-whats-
real-and-what-isnt/) new legislation that [tightened the state’s voter ID
rules](https://idahocapitalsun.com/2026/02/25/under-idaho-bill-poll-workers-
would-try-to-verify-more-voter-identities/), though he did
[oppose](https://www.idahostatesman.com/news/politics-government/state-
politics/article299638629.html) an even more aggressive version of the law. He
has also [rejected](https://idahocapitalsun.com/2026/04/01/trump-
administration-sues-idaho-election-official-to-force-him-to-turn-over-
sensitive-voter-data/) the Trump administration’s request for sensitive voter
rolls information.

![](https://boltsmag.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/McGrane.jpg)Idaho
Secretary of State Phil McGrane is seeking a second term (McGrane/Facebook)

McGrane is heavily favored to win a second term in one of the nation's reddest
states. He faces a [rematch](https://idahocapitalsun.com/2022/10/28/in-idahos-
secretary-of-state-race-one-candidate-has-support-from-both-sides/) against
Democrat Shawn Keenan, whom he defeated 72 to 27 percent in 2022.

### **Illinois**

**Via election** **for governor**

Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias, a Democrat, is heavily favored against
Diane Harris, his [GOP
challenger](https://www.shawlocal.com/news/2026/08/08/joliet-gop-candidate-
for-secretary-of-state-hopes-to-capitalize-on-giannoulias-run-for-chicago-
mayor/); in fact, he has already announced he’s campaigning for [Chicago mayor
in 2027](https://www.hpherald.com/evening_digest/secretary-of-state-alexi-
giannoulias-enters-crowded-mayors-
race/article_d1c00011-627c-455a-a875-5b7b34d52fc5.html). .

But the Illinois secretary of state is [not involved in election
administration](https://boltsmag.org/whats-on-the-ballot/local-election-
administration/#IL). Instead, elections are overseen by an eight-person board
of elections. Board members are appointed by the governor, but they must be
equally split between the two major parties and
[confirmed](https://www.ilga.gov/Legislation/BillStatus?DocNum=1040206&DocTypeID=AM&GAID=18&LegID=163701&SessionID=114)
by the state Senate. That structure tempers how much the winner of the
governor’s race—Democratic incumbent J.B. Pritzker is favored over Republican
Darren Bailey—might alter election administration.

### **Indiana**

**Via election for secretary of state**

Diego Morales won the secretary of state race four years ago on a
[campaign](https://boltsmag.org/guide-to-2022-secretary-of-state-
elections/#IN) of election denialism, and his tenure as secretary of state was
marked by [controversy](https://indianacapitalchronicle.com/2025/06/19/budget-
committee-members-lob-questions-at-embattled-secretary-of-state-diego-
morales/) nearly from the start; he raised questions after using taxpayer
money to buy an expensive vehicle, taking international trips that blurred his
professional and private lives, and hiring at least one family member to a
post in his office. In June, he lost his reelection bid at a GOP convention
when Republicans nominated Max Engling, a former staffer for U.S. Senator Jim
Banks.

Engling faces a crowded field that includes Libertarian Lauri Shillings and
Greg Ballard, the former Republican mayor of Indianapolis who is now running
as an independent and [arguing](https://fox59.com/indianapolitics/greg-
ballard-calls-for-changes-to-make-indiana-sec-of-state-position-nonpartisan/)
that the secretary of state should be an entirely non-partisan office.
Democrats nominated Beau Bayh, an attorney who has never held office but has
roots in a political dynasty—his
[grandfather](https://www.wfyi.org/shows/birch-bayh-american-senator) is
former three-term U.S. Senator Birch Bayh, and his father is former Indiana
Governor and U.S. Senator Evan Bayh—and has
[raised](https://www.transparencyusa.org/in/race/indiana-secretary-of-
state-76694) far more than the other candidates.

### **Iowa**

**Via election for secretary of state**

Republican Paul Pate, Iowa’s secretary of state since 2015, seeks a fourth
term in office, and is challenged this year by Democrat Ryan Peterman, a
former Navy pilot.

![](https://boltsmag.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/10/672670505_1325203409425234_1610678916059101672_n.jpg)Iowa
Secretary of State Paul Pate visits a local elections office in Polk County
(photo via Iowa secretary of state/Facebook).

In Pate’s time in office, Iowa’s GOP-run legislature has, with his blessing,
significantly restricted voter access, including by giving voters less time to
request mail ballots; installed a strict deadline that says mail ballots won’t
be counted if received after polls close, even if they were mailed before
Election Day; and cut the state’s early-voting period in half.

Peterman wants to expand voter access, including by [restoring more time for
early voting](https://iowacapitaldispatch.com/2026/08/15/secretary-of-state-
candidate-ryan-peterman-calls-for-election-changes/). He couldn’t do that on
his own, however; even if he wins, he’ll have to contend with the same GOP-
controlled legislature that passed the restrictions he opposes.

### **Kansas**

**Via election for secretary of state**

Kansas last year [banned grace periods](https://boltsmag.org/restrictions-on-
grace-periods-for-mail-ballots/) for mail ballots that are postmarked by
Election Day but arrive later, one of several GOP-led states to do so since
Trump’s return to power. The lead sponsor of that bill, Pat Proctor, is now
the GOP’s candidate for secretary of state, running to replace incumbent Scott
Schwab, a Republican who unsuccessfully ran for governor.

“If it was up to me, Election Day would be Election Day,” Proctor said in a
leaked video obtained by the Kansas advocacy group Loud Light and
[published](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0X7MLXASbWE) by _Kansas
Reflector_. “There wouldn’t be early voting. Mail-in ballots would only be for
military or severely disabled.”

Proctor is running against Democrat Jennifer Day, another former state
legislator [who says she](https://lawrencekstimes.com/2026/08/03/kns-sos-
candidates-2608/) wants to see the state’s three-day grace period reinstated.
The elimination of that grace period, she and many voting rights advocates
believe, was especially impactful in Kansas because it already has a much
shorter early-voting window than most other states.

### **Maine**

**Via state legislative elections**

Maine’s secretary of state is appointed by the legislature, not elected, and
so this office’s future depends on the outcome of November’s elections, when
every seat in the statehouse will be on the ballot. Democrats currently hold
both legislative chambers, but Republicans need to flip only a few seats in
each venue to retake control.

The current secretary of state, Democrat Shenna Bellows, told _Bolts_ that she
intends to seek another term as secretary when the legislature convenes.

![](https://boltsmag.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/10/26030773855583-scaled.jpg)The secretaries of state of
Vermont (Sarah Copeland Hanzas), Maine (Shenna Bellows), and Rhode Island
(Gregg Amore) are here standing at a conference in Washington, D.C., in
January 2026. (AP Photo/Cliff Owen)

Bellows, who this year ran unsuccessfully for governor, then ran
unsuccessfully in the brief scramble to replace Graham Platner in the U.S.
Senate race, has opposed Trump’s attacks on election administration. She told
the Department of Justice to “[jump in the Gulf of
Maine](https://mainemorningstar.com/2025/07/29/trump-administration-requested-
voter-data-secretary-bellows-says-go-jump-in-the-gulf-of-maine/)” when it
sought Maine voter-roll information. Last year, she also fought [proposals
that would have restricted mail voting](https://boltsmag.org/maine-
question-1-in-november-2025-mail-voting/), and which Mainers ended up
[rejecting](https://boltsmag.org/five-ways-2025-elections-affect-voting-rules-
and-democracy/). “We should not be making it harder for people to have their
voices heard,” she told _Bolts_.

In this state with a [tradition](https://www.pressherald.com/2026/04/15/does-
maine-have-one-of-the-highest-voter-participation-rates-nationwide-fact-
brief/) of high voter turnout, voters remain who have trouble getting their
voices heard. Unlike almost every other part of the country, people imprisoned
over felony convictions have the right to vote in Maine, but, as [_Bolts_
reported this summer](https://boltsmag.org/maine-prison-voting-rights/),
significant access gaps remain for incarcerated voters. Bellows’ office has
disappointed some voting rights advocates on this front, including by refusing
to establish polling places inside prisons.

### **Maryland  **

**Via election for governor**

Maryland’s governor appoints the secretary of state. Current office-holder
Susan Lee was chosen by Democrat Wes Moore in January 2023.

Moore is up for reelection and is heavily favored against Dan Cox, a
Republican who already lost to Moore by over 30 points in
[2022](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2022/11/08/us/elections/results-
maryland.html). Cox falsely denied Trump’s loss in the 2020 election and
[helped organize bus travel](https://marylandmatters.org/2021/01/07/del-cox-
arranged-buses-to-violent-trump-rally-calls-vice-president-a-traitor/) to D.C.
on Jan. 6, 2021, for people demanding that the result be overturned. Even if
Cox were to score a massive upset in ousting Moore, his nominee would still
need to be confirmed by the solidly Democratic state Senate.

### **Massachusetts**

**Via election for secretary of state  **

Bill Galvin, a Democrat, has been in office since 1995 and has [occasionally
frustrated progressives](https://boltsmag.org/massachusetts-secretary-of-
state-galvin-sullivan/) who wanted more ambitious expansions of ballot access.

This year, he is [running for a _ninth_
term](https://commonwealthbeacon.org/politics/a-cakewalk-for-bill-galvin/)
entirely unopposed. Massachusetts voters still face important decisions that
will shape elections; [Galvin has led the
effort](https://commonwealthbeacon.org/politics/galvin-pursuing-ballot-
question-on-same-day-voter-registration/) to advance a measure on the November
ballot to allow people to register to vote on Election Day.

### **Michigan**

**Via election for secretary of state**

Michigan Democrats are hoping to play a game of musical chairs with the
state’s top offices: Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson is running to take
Gretchen Whitmer’s place as governor, and running to take Benson’s slot is
Lieutenant Governor Garlin Gilchrist, who says his experience as a former
software engineer could help him ensure that elections are secure.

Gilchrist faces Republican Anthony Forlini, the clerk in Macomb County, a
populous Detroit suburban area. Forlini has put a spotlight on claims of voter
fraud, conducting a “forensic audit” of the 2020 election [that found no
evidence of impropriety](https://michiganadvance.com/2022/01/11/gop-initiated-
forensic-audit-unveils-no-fraud-in-macomb-county-election/), and more recently
[bypassing state
officials](https://www.votebeat.org/michigan/2026/05/19/anthony-forlini-
federal-government-noncitizen-voters-secretary-of-state-candidate/) and
working with Trump administration databases to track down noncitizens on voter
rolls. Now he points to his years of election administration experience as
reasons why voters should count on him to be even-keeled; he [got the GOP
nomination](https://www.votebeat.org/michigan/2026/03/28/republican-
convention-nominates-anthony-forlini-secretary-of-state-2026-election/) over a
candidate who was much more outspoken about her election denialism, in a
[departure](https://boltsmag.org/kristina-karamo-has-plans-to-unwind-michigan-
elections-secretary-of-state/) for this state party. But Forlini [declined to
answer](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pilD84-H3Ek&t=815s) in a September
interview when asked who won the 2020 presidential election. In interviews
with [_Votebeat_ in
October](https://www.votebeat.org/michigan/2026/10/08/garlin-gilchrist-
anthony-forlini-secretary-of-state-2026-election/), Gilchrist said he would
not share the state’s unredacted voter rolls with the Trump administration
while Forlini said he’d consider it.

### **Minnesota**

**Via election for secretary of state**

Incumbent Steve Simon, a Democrat, is seeking another term against Republican
Tad Jude, a former state legislator and district court judge. Simon is
defending his tenure as elections chief of a state that regularly has one of
the highest voter turnout rates in the country; he refused to share sensitive
voter information with the Trump administration [and prevailed in
court](https://www.courthousenews.com/judge-rejects-doj-reach-for-minnesota-
voter-data/).  

Jude, meanwhile, has called his platform “SAVE Minnesota,” a name that mirrors
the Trump-championed SAVE Act, the federal legislation that would require
documentary proof of citizenship for people to register to vote. He also
[says](https://www.kaxe.org/2026-09-28/secretary-of-state-jude-kuhlstennes-
simon-tangen-mn-2026-election-guide) he’d want to use the Trump
administration’s controversial [SAVE voter
database](https://www.scotusblog.com/2026/09/supreme-court-clears-way-for-
trump-administration-to-use-modified-voter-verification-database/) to confirm
citizenship. Jude says there’s a [need to tighten voting
rules](https://www.kttc.com/2026/07/24/one-on-one-republican-minnesota-
secretary-state-candidate-tad-jude/) to fight fraud, including requiring photo
ID for every voter.

### **Nebraska**

**Via election for secretary of state**

Secretary of State Bob Evnen, a Republican, has done a whole lot to curry
favor in the GOP. Among other things, he teamed with the state’s attorney
general to [shut down voting rights](https://boltsmag.org/nebraska-voting-
rights-restoration/) for people with past felonies; he tried to [kick a
Democrat off the ballot](https://nebraskaexaminer.com/2026/03/17/evnen-
removes-nebraska-democratic-u-s-senate-candidate-burbank-from-ballot/) for
U.S. Senate; and he complied with, and then
[downplayed](https://sos.nebraska.gov/sites/default/files/doc/news-
releases/Secretary%20Evnen%20sends%20information%20from%20Nebraska%20voter%20registration%20list%20to%20the%20Department%20of%20Justice_0.pdf?fbclid=IwY2xjawUslV1leHRuA2FlbQIxMABwZG9mBWJyaWQRMTZLQ0N0UVhpRmdhaVFqdjJzcnRjBmFwcF9pZBAyMjIwMzkxNzg4MjAwODkyAAEe8uIAkZOmi-
FXPugE-8AOIVoceez5OmeLvf_wmhBCu3LvQ8CGT6tUaCdx_yE_aem_Ryhff4lB0lzws5jyzMMZfA),
the DOJ’s controversial request for Nebraska’s voter data.

None of this was enough to protect Evnen in the GOP primary earlier this year,
when he lost to a challenger from the right, Scott Petersen, a businessman and
self-described “America First Republican” who echoes election conspiracies and
[calls for](https://www.petersenfornebraska.com/plan) a “DOGE approach to
government.” If elected, he says, that approach would include a “top-to-bottom
audit” of the secretary of state office and subsequent elimination of as-yet-
unspecified roles or expenses.

Petersen faces Democrat Sarah Slattery, [who runs a winery and event
space](https://svevineyards.com), in November. Slattery says she wants to
expand voter access, including by advocating for same-day voter registration,
and she opposes strict [voter ID
rules](https://sos.nebraska.gov/sites/default/files/doc/Feb%202024%20Voter%20ID%20Brochure%20English%20with%20SM.pdf)
adopted in 2023. Even in a potential blue wave year, she faces long odds:
Nebraska hasn’t elected a Democrat as secretary of state since 1933.

Potentially altering this race is the presence of an unusually prominent
third-party candidate: Bob Krist, a former Republican state senator who ran
for governor as a Democrat and is now running for secretary of state under the
banner of Nebraska’s America First Party. Krist told the _Nebraska Examiner_
that he [thought voters needed another
option](https://nebraskaexaminer.com/2026/09/01/former-state-sen-bob-krist-
selects-america-first-party-for-secretary-of-state-run/) who would push back
against Petersen’s criticism of state elections.

### **Nevada**

**Via election for secretary of state**

Jim Marchant, the Republican nominee for secretary of state, is an election
denier who has called for reforms that stand out even in the modern GOP. He
not only supports ending universal mail voting and electronic voting, but
[says](https://apnews.com/article/nevada-secretary-of-state-election-
conspiracies-marchant-988849972274838c21ca3fbbd73bdd90) that if he’s elected
he’ll push to unregister Nevadans en masse, and allow reregistration only by
those verified as eligible.

_The Nevada Independent_ [reported earlier this
year](https://thenevadaindependent.com/article/should-nevada-elections-be-
overhauled-heres-what-gop-secretary-of-state-hopefuls-say) that Marchant has
even floated using heartbeat detection in that verification process. Numerous
elections experts told _Bolts_ that they had not heard of such a proposal
before, and the Marchant campaign didn’t respond to repeated requests for
comment from _Bolts_ on the proposal.

![](https://boltsmag.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/10/475691813_1012661310684175_6674934093261316483_n.jpg)Jim
Marchant, here shown alongside President Trump, is running for secretary of
state for the second time (photo via Marchant campaign/Facebook)

He has long been a proud, vocal promoter of the lie that the 2020 presidential
election was stolen from Trump, and he [led a national slate of
candidates](https://boltsmag.org/guide-to-2022-secretary-of-state-
elections/#NV) in 2022 who ran on that message. He ended up [narrowly
losing](https://boltsmag.org/secretary-of-state-races-election-deniers-
results/) to Democrat Cisco Aguilar, an attorney and former staffer for
longtime U.S. Senator Harry Reid. These two face off in a rematch this year.

As secretary, Aguilar has been a frontline defender against Trump’s attempted
federal takeover of state election administration. He’s the chair of the
Democratic Association of Secretaries of State, and he has called Trump’s
election conspiracies “some bullshit.” [_Bolts_ interviewed Aguilar in
2023](https://boltsmag.org/nevada-election-workers-harassment-secretary-of-
state/), when he voiced concern that these conspiracies were subjecting
election workers to harassment and endangering election administration.

### **New Hampshire**

**Via elections for state legislature**

Legislators vote to select the New Hampshire secretary of state every two
years. In late 2022 and 2024, they chose Republican David Scanlan.

Scanlan has supported the New Hampshire GOP’s recent election reforms,
including [restrictions ](https://www.nhpr.org/nh-news/2022-04-20/citing-
voter-integrity-concerns-state-house-republicans-aim-to-pass-major-overhaul-
of-same-day-registration-process)on same-day voter registration and a [strict
proof of citizenship requirement](https://boltsmag.org/new-hampshire-
republicans-proof-of-citizenship-to-register-to-vote/) to register to vote.
But he [also rejected](https://www.nhpr.org/nh-news/2025-07-16/nh-secretary-
of-state-rebuffs-trump-administration-request-for-states-voter-roll) Trump’s
request for sensitive voter information, [sparking](https://www.nhpr.org/nh-
news/2025-09-25/trump-administration-sues-new-hampshire-over-access-to-voter-
data) a lawsuit from the Department of Justice, and criticized Trump's [effort
to dictate](https://www.nhpr.org/nh-news/2026-04-01/nh-secretary-of-state-
scanlan-trump-administration-elections-voter-data-absentee-voting) how
elections should be run.

Scanlan’s office told _Bolts_ that he would seek another two-year term in
December. Control of the legislature is uncertain but there’s no guarantee
that Democrats would opt for an alternative even if they flip the legislature.
He got support from [many crossover
Democrats](https://www.wmur.com/article/scanlan-new-hampshire-secretary-of-
state-election-12722/42181924) in his run in late 2022, and in late 2024, when
the GOP enjoyed larger majorities, [no one challenged
him](https://www.wmur.com/article/david-scanlan-re-elected-secretary-of-
state-120424/63099505).

### **New Mexico**

**Via election for secretary of state**

New Mexico has [passed several reforms easing ballot access and voter
registration](https://boltsmag.org/new-mexico-voting-rights-package/) with
support from Secretary of State Maggie Toulouse Oliver, including a law in
2023 that restored voting rights to anyone not currently incarcerated. But a
year after that reform, formerly incarcerated voters who’d had their rights
restored were still struggling to access those rights and [_Bolts_ reported
that](https://boltsmag.org/voting-rights-restoration-reform-in-new-mexico/)
Toulouse Oliver’s office was instructing county clerks to only accept
registrations from formerly incarcerated voters in person, not by mail or
online. The state reached a settlement in late 2024 with voters who sued over
the registration issues.

Now two years later, Toulouse Oliver is term-limited, and Democrats have
nominated a local elections administrator to replace her: Amanda López Askin,
who currently serves as the clerk of Doña Ana County and touts her experience
as an elections official. López Askin, who once faced [death
threats](https://sourcenm.com/2024/04/16/southern-n-m-officials-grapple-with-
threats-raising-questions-about-local-democracy/) from a disgruntled
candidate, says she’d [fight federal
incursions](https://sourcenm.com/2026/04/29/new-mexico-primary-2026-secretary-
of-state/) in elections.

López Askin faces Republican Ramona Goolsby, who wants to [roll
back](https://www.santafenewmexican.com/news/elections/republican-ramona-
goolsby-shares-her-priorities-in-campaign-for-n-m-secretary-of-
state/article_0abce68a-4297-4843-9f09-73950ac44057.html) some of New Mexico’s
recent reforms, including the state’s permanent absentee voter list that was
[set up in 2024](https://apnews.com/article/new-mexico-streamlines-absentee-
ballot-requests-f12bc284e517145ae90fa5360be0b106). Asked by the _Santa Fe New
Mexican_ who won the 2020 presidential election, Goolsby never answered and
said there were “issues” with mail voting. Asked in a follow-up if she thinks
the election was stolen from Trump, she said that she had asked questions but
that, “overall, I can't say that I find it (stolen).”

### **New York**

**Via election for governor**

New York elections [are run](https://boltsmag.org/whats-on-the-ballot/local-
election-administration/#NY) by the State Board of Elections, a bipartisan
body whose members are named by the governor. (The governor _also_ appoints
the secretary of state, but that office has no duties relating to election
administration.) The board [drew a
lawsuit](https://www.localsyr.com/news/state-news/inside-the-justice-
department-case-against-new-york-over-voter-rolls/) from the Trump
administration this year for refusing to hand over sensitive voter data to
federal authorities; a court [tossed the
lawsuit](https://campaignlegal.org/press-releases/victory-new-york-voters-
federal-court-dismisses-doj-lawsuit-seeking-private-voter), siding with New
York’s board, this summer.

![](https://boltsmag.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/10/836515354_1119391027779194_2094885297914206641_n-e1791580621866.jpg)Bruce
Blakeman, the GOP nominee for governor in New York, is here pictured at a
campaign event (photo via Blakeman campaign/Facebook).

Governor Kathy Hochul is running for reelection this fall against Bruce
Blakeman, the Nassau County executive who has [sowed
doubt](https://www.cityandstateny.com/politics/2026/07/blakeman-sets-stage-
election-denialism/415103/) about elections by accusing state Democrats of
cheating to defeat him and threatening them with jail time.

### **North Dakota**

**Via election for secretary of state**

In 2023, the Eighth Circuit of Appeals shattered decades of precedent and
ruled that private individuals and third-party groups are not allowed to sue
over violations of Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, which bans
discrimination on the basis of race.

The startling decision involved a case out of Arkansas. But North Dakota
Secretary of State Michael Howe asked the appeals court to use that same
finding to overturn a court ruling that struck down North Dakota legislative
maps for violating the rights of Native voters. The Eighth Circuit agreed, as
[_Bolts_ reported in 2025](https://boltsmag.org/voting-rights-act-natives-
north-dakota/); it effectively held that tribes in North Dakota cannot sue the
state for violating the VRA.

“It means the Voting Rights Act is functionally dead in a vast part of our
country,” Samantha Blencke, an attorney with the Native American Rights Fund,
told _Bolts_ at the time. (Since then, the U.S. Supreme Court has struck
another, [near-fatal blow](https://boltsmag.org/scotus-callais-voting-rights-
act-ask-bolts/) to the VRA in a separate case.)

Howe is running for a second term this year against Ryan Braunberger, a
Democratic state senator who
[says](https://www.newsdakota.com/2026/07/27/government-transparency-ai-data-
centers-hot-topics-in-valley-city/) the state should adopt an independent
redistricting commission. Braunberger did not answer a request for comment on
his views on the VRA legislation.

### **Ohio**

**Via election for secretary of state**

Ohio Republicans, including Secretary of State Frank LaRose, have taken steps
to make voting more difficult and to [obey Trump’s election
wishes](https://boltsmag.org/ohio-secretary-of-state/). For one, LaRose
[complied](https://ohiocapitaljournal.com/2026/03/11/secretary-of-state-frank-
larose-gives-8-million-ohio-voters-information-to-trump-justice-department/)
with a Department of Justice request by handing over the state’s voter rolls
earlier this year, in contrast to many of his counterparts around the country.
With LaRose’s support, Ohio [also recently banned](https://boltsmag.org/ohio-
ends-grace-periods-for-mail-ballots/) its grace period for mail ballots.

![](https://boltsmag.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/10/24255533404284-scaled.jpg)Ohio Secretary of State
Frank LaRose, left, speaks with Arizona Secretary of State Adrian Fontes,
before a hearing at the House Administration Committee on Sept. 11, 2024.
(Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call via AP Images)  

LaRose is barred from seeking a third term, and Treasurer Robert Sprague is
the Republican nominee to replace him. Sprague, like LaRose, is vocal about
[combatting non-citizen voter
fraud](https://x.com/RobertCSprague/status/2100727746385117639?s=20), despite
overwhelming evidence that it hardly exists. Sprague [also
says](https://www.wvxu.org/politics/2026-04-30/analysis-fact-check-robert-
sprague-tv-ad-ballot-drop-boxes) he will support Trump by looking to eliminate
dropboxes for mail ballots.

He faces Democrat Allison Russo, a state representative who says Ohio’s
elections are “already safe and secure,” voted against the bill to bar the
grace period, and recently
[posted](https://x.com/Russo4Ohio/status/2077951707456127295?s=20) on social
media, “President Trump continues to focus on debunked conspiracies and
election lies in order to cling to power.”

### **Oklahoma**

****Via election for governor****

In Oklahoma, the governor gets to appoint the members of the state board of
elections, [who then run](https://boltsmag.org/whats-on-the-ballot/local-
election-administration/#OK) Oklahoma elections. (The secretary of state does
not oversee elections here.) This year, the board initially resisted the Trump
administration’s request to hand over sensitive voter information. But
[Oklahoma's attorney general later negotiated](https://www.kgou.org/oklahoma-
voter-data-to-feds) with federal agencies, with the board's approval, to share
the data in a manner that they say shields voters' privacy.

A Trump ally, former state Senator Mike Mazzei, is now the Republican nominee
for governor; he faces Democrat Cyndi Munson, a state representative. The
effect of their race on the elections board will be somewhat mitigated by the
fact that governors must pick a bipartisan board; they must choose one of the
three members from a list provided by the opposing major party. In addition,
the governor’s nominees must be confirmed by the state legislature.

### **Pennsylvania**

**Via election for governor**

In Pennsylvania, the secretary of state is appointed by the governor; that
power became a defining issue in the 2022 governor’s race when the GOP

secretary-of-state-pick-disrupt-pennsylvania-elections/) who explicitly said
he would select a like-minded secretary of state. But Democrat Josh Shapiro
won that race, and then appointed Al Schmidt, a Philadelphia Republican who
had denounced efforts to discourage voting, to oversee Pennsylvania elections.

![](https://boltsmag.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/10/763881179_1604126048423721_5962465093166454261_n.jpg)Pennsylvania
Secretary of State Al Schmidt was appointed by Governor Josh Shapiro, who is
seeking reelection this fall (photo via Pennsylvania Department of
State/Facebook)

Shapiro and Schmidt have since implemented reforms meant to ease [mail
voting](https://www.votebeat.org/pennsylvania/2024/05/31/mail-ballot-
rejections-2024-primary-election-envelope-redesign/) and voter
[registration](https://www.pa.gov/governor/newsroom/2023-press-
releases/governor-shapiro-implements-automatic-voter-registration-in-penn);
they’ve also both [pushed back](https://penncapital-star.com/election-2026/us-
supreme-court-ruling-provides-much-need-finality-on-mail-voting-in-pa/)
against Trump’s efforts to change voting procedures.

Shapiro is now running for reelection against Republican Stacy Garrity, the
state treasurer. Garrity’s campaign did not reply to a request for comment on
how she would approach the choice of a secretary of state; a review of her
record by [_Votebeat_](https://www.votebeat.org/pennsylvania/2026/08/20/josh-
shapiro-stacy-garrity-governor-2026-midterm-election-policy) found that she
said in 2022 that Trump won the 2020 election, and this year she again claimed
there were “irregularities” in Trump’s loss that year.

### **Rhode Island**

**Via election for secretary of state  **

Secretary of State Gregg Amore, a Democrat, is running for reelection
unopposed. In fact, his Republican opponent in the
[2022](https://boltsmag.org/guide-to-2022-secretary-of-state-elections/#RI)
election [attended](https://rhodeislandcurrent.com/2026/03/11/flanked-by-
labor-and-democratic-leaders-ri-secretary-of-state-gregg-amore-kicks-off-
reelection-bid/) the launch of his reelection campaign.

Amore’s first term was marked by his repeated but fruitless
[advocacy](https://www.bostonglobe.com/2023/01/12/metro/secretary-state-gregg-
amore-makes-case-same-day-voter-registration/) for state lawmakers to adopt
[same-day voter
registration](https://rhodeislandcurrent.com/2024/01/19/proponents-rally-for-
same-day-voter-registration/), a reform that their neighbors in Massachusetts
are voting on this fall. Rhode Island has among the nation’s [most
restrictive](https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/voter-registration-
deadlines) registration deadlines, with a cutoff 30 days before an election.

### **South Carolina**

**Via election for governor**

The secretary of state’s office doesn’t oversee elections in South Carolina.
Instead, the governor names five members to the State Election Commission.

The governor’s race this fall pits Attorney General Alan Wilson, a Republican,
against state Representative Jermaine Johnson, a Democrat. Wilson in 2020
[joined](https://www.scag.gov/about-the-office/news/ag-alan-wilson-s-
statement-on-texas-election-lawsuit/) some other attorneys general in
supporting a lawsuit that [sought to
overturn](https://www.postandcourier.com/politics/sc-attorney-general-wilson-
faces-disciplinary-complaint-over-supporting-election-
lawsuit/article_b3b6ce68-54ef-11eb-8efb-1766456a358f.html) the presidential
results in four states, and this year he backed Trump’s bid to [force
stringent new rules](https://www.scag.gov/about-the-office/news/attorney-
general-alan-wilson-defends-president-trump-s-executive-order-on-election-
integrity/) on how states run elections.

### **South Dakota**

**Via election for secretary of state**

Republican incumbent Monae Johnson was ousted this summer after just one term
as secretary of state. In her first run in 2022, Johnson expressed skepticism
about the results of the 2020 election, consistent with other election
deniers; she then encountered a number of issues during her time in office,
including a [lawsuit](https://southdakotasearchlight.com/2026/09/15/lawsuit-
causes-south-dakota-secretary-of-state-to-issue-new-guidance-on-federal-only-
voter-notices/) over her management of voter registration and primary
elections this summer that a local election official
[described](https://southdakotasearchlight.com/2026/04/16/absolute-chaos-
state-local-officials-disagree-on-path-forward-amid-delay-in-early-voting/) as
“absolute chaos.”

Then, in the GOP convention in June, Johnson was passed over for an even more
conservative challenger, Heather Baxter, a state representative who [wants
to](https://southdakotasearchlight.com/2026/06/27/states-top-election-
official-loses-nomination-to-challenger-who-supports-hand-counting/) hand
count ballots, a longtime [priority](https://boltsmag.org/new-mexico-election-
conspiracies-trujillo/) for legislators on the far right. In a twist, Johnson
has since endorsed Democratic nominee Terrence Davis,
[writing](https://dakotawarcollege.com/a-personal-statement-from-monae-l-
johnson-south-dakota-secretary-of-state-why-i-am-supporting-terrence-davis-
guest-column/) in a local news outlet: “South Dakota deserves a Secretary of
State who will strengthen confidence through performance rather than
provocation.”

### **Texas**

**Via election for governor**

Should Gina Hinojosa defeat GOP Governor Greg Abbott in November, that would
come with a bonus prize: choosing a secretary of state, which in Texas is an
appointed position. Abbott in July chose a new secretary, [senior adviser and
longtime Republican Robert
Howden](https://www.votebeat.org/texas/2026/07/17/robert-howden-appointed-
texas-secretary-of-state-midterms-2026/). Howden’s early tenure has been
marked by revelations, first [reported by
_Votebeat_](https://www.votebeat.org/texas/2026/09/26/voter-registration-
delay-backlog-online-dps-error/), that the Department of Public Safety has
mishandled and delayed thousands of voter registration applications and
[accusations that the secretary of state’s
office](https://www.votebeat.org/texas/2026/09/24/dps-voter-registration-
applications-error-paul-bettencourt-team/) failed to catch the issue.

![](https://boltsmag.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/10/25206655190029-scaled.jpg)Gina Hinojosa, a Texas
lawmaker who is running for governor, speaks during a rally to protest against
redistricting on July 24, 2025. (AP Photo/Eric Gay)

Voting rights have been a major partisan faultline in Texas, a state that
still doesn’t even have [online voter
registration](https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/online-voter-
registration). GOP lawmakers have passed laws that prevent local election
officials from expanding ballot access, [restricting the range of reforms
county-level administrators can pursue](https://boltsmag.org/voting-rights-
advocates-search-for-openings-to-go-local-in-texas/), but a secretary of state
would have plenty of authority to make Texas procedures more inclusive. As a
state lawmaker, Hinojosa has [filed
bills](https://www.texastribune.org/2022/10/28/texas-young-voter-turnout-
access) to make voting more accessible and she has stressed that theme [in her
governor’s campaign](https://stylemagazine.com/news/2026/jun/02/gina-hinojosa-
houston-campaign-stop-education-economy-and-voting-rights-focus).

But one limiting factor on Hinojosa would be that the Texas Senate, which is
likely to remain Republican, would have to confirm her nominee.

### **Vermont**

**Via election for secretary of state  **

This is the third consecutive cycle in which Secretary of State Sarah Copeland
Hanzas, a Democrat, faces H. Brooke Paige, a Republican who [has followed
Trump](https://www.facebook.com/brooke.paige.395/posts/pfbid0LMtGkhbGknMqTbHAAvKU5YSRdarM5jg2yMXftDLnzwsf6w3kM1DsZ6e4sVThE1J7l)
in baselessly claiming that the 2020 presidential race was “stolen.”

Copeland Hanzas defeated Paige by 30 points in 2022 and then by 19 points in
2024. “It is highly worrisome to hear people echoing false claims and
misinformation about the safety and security of our elections,” Copeland
Hanzas [told _Bolts_ ](https://boltsmag.org/vermont-secretary-of-state/)during
her first run. “The purpose of these claims is to discourage people from
participating in elections.”

### **Washington, D.C.**

**Via election for mayor**

Elections here are overseen by a three-member board, appointed by the mayor
and confirmed by the city council. D.C. is about to elect a new mayor, and
Democratic nominee Janeese Lewis George, a progressive councilmember, is all
but guaranteed to win in this overwhelmingly liberal city.

D.C. has taken significant steps to make voting easier in recent years,
including through a [first-in-the-nation
reform](https://boltsmag.org/washington-dc-bill-voter-registration/) to create
a list of “preapproved” voters that largely eliminates the need for any voter
registration. As with other local policy matters, D.C. election officials must
contend with a Congress that has been frequently hostile to its self-
determination, [including on voter eligibility in the
District](https://www.washingtonpost.com/dc-md-va/2025/06/10/house-vote-dc-
laws-police-reform-noncitizen-voting/).

### **Wisconsin**

**Via multiple state elections**

The Wisconsin secretary of state does not oversee election administration;
that job belongs to the six-member bipartisan Wisconsin Elections Commission
and their administrator. The commission was thrown into chaos several years
ago when Republicans in the state legislature tried to force Meagan Wolfe, the
commission’s nonpartisan administrator, out of her job [after she became a
target of right-wing conspiracies](https://boltsmag.org/wisconsin-election-
administrator-republicans-election-denier-conspiracies-state-supreme-court/).
They even got to the brink of impeaching her, but the state supreme court
[ruled](https://www.wpr.org/news/wisconsin-supreme-court-rules-meagan-wolfe-
can-remain-states-top-elections-official) unanimously in 2025 that she could
stay in the role.

If Wolfe leaves, her successor would be chosen by the elections commission,
whose members [are appointed by](https://boltsmag.org/whats-on-the-
ballot/local-election-administration/#WI) the governor and legislative
leaders. Wisconsinites are electing their governor and most of their lawmakers
this year in some of the nation’s most closely-watched contests, which have
both parties hoping for full control. In the governor’s race, GOP nominee Tom
Tiffany, a U.S. representative who [backed Trump’s
efforts](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/gop-governor-
candidates-cast-doubt-2020-election-changing-tune-rcna596630) to overturn the
2020 presidential election, faces Democratic Milwaukee County Executive David
Crowley, who in his past stint as a state lawmaker [proposed
reforms](https://www.wpr.org/politics/wisconsin-democrats-push-automatic-
voter-registration) meant to ease voting such as automatic voter registration.

Some Republicans want to shift election administration to the secretary of
state’s office. Republican Jay Schroeder, a self-described “authentic MAGA
activist,” [is running on doing away
](https://wisconsinexaminer.com/2026/08/11/maga-activist-who-wants-to-
eliminate-elections-commission-wins-gop-nod-for-secretary-of-state/)with this
commission entirely; his Democratic opponent JoCasta Zamarripa [told local
media](https://www.ehextra.com/news/zamarripa-pledges-modernization-advocacy-
in-seeking-wisconsin-secretary-of-state-
post/article_99a263b5-2336-4660-957c-c9580eb7aae0.html) that she believes that
electoral oversight should remain with the commission.

### **Wyoming**

**Via election for secretary of state  **

Far-right Republicans who want to crack down on elections suffered a heavy
defeat in the GOP’s August primaries, [_Bolts_
reported](https://boltsmag.org/wyoming-gop-primary-secretary-of-state-freedom-
caucus/). The winner in the secretary of state race, Robert Short, says that
the state has no rampant voter fraud problem, that he wants to protect mail
voting and ballot drop boxes from right-wing attacks, and that he’ll work to
set up online voter registration.

![](https://boltsmag.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/08/722768375_122113019433207742_1521041636579799200_n.jpg)Robert
Short is the GOP nominee for Wyoming secretary of state. (Facebook/Short for
State)

Short told _Bolts_ he supports “whatever we can do to make voter registration
and access to the ballot easier.”

Short now faces Democrat Bryan McCarty, who is making the case that voters
should reject Republican candidates due to Trump’s attacks on democracy; Short
is favored in this deeply red state. The winner will replace Chuck Gray, an
election denier who [pushed for harsh new
restrictions](https://boltsmag.org/wyoming-voter-registration-proof-of-
citizenship-law/) during his one term in office and who is now running for a
congressional seat.

## **What about the 15 other states?**

In nine states, voters will elect their chief elections official in 2027
(Kentucky, Louisiana, and Mississippi) or 2028 (Missouri, Montana, Oregon,
Utah, Washington, and West Virginia).

In Delaware, North Carolina, and Tennessee, the elections officials will be
chosen after the 2028 elections by whomever wins other state offices—the
governor, the auditor, and the legislature, respectively. And in New Jersey
and Virginia, the next choice will come down to whomever wins the governorship
in 2029.

In Hawaii, finally, elections are overseen by a director appointed by a
bipartisan commission; the sitting director’s term ends in early 2028 but no
board member’s term is due to expire before then.
